messages.text: Furious Arteta rages over 'unacceptable' Sunderland penalty call

metadata.summary: A furious Mikel Arteta described Sunderland's penalty in Arsenal's 2-0 win at the Stadium of Light as "unacceptable".
metadata.content: Mikel Arteta rages at Sunderland penalty decision after Arsenal win at Stadium of Light: 'This cannot happen' | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Mikel Arteta rages at Sunderland penalty decision after Arsenal win at Stadium of Light: 'This cannot happen' Mikel Arteta was left furious by the award of Sunderland's penalty during Arsenal's 2-0 win at the Stadium of Light, saying such decisions can cost a side a Premier League title; David Raya saved Enzo Le Fee's spot kick as Gunners claimed a fourth straight win Nick Wright Football Features Writer @nicholaspwright Saturday 12 September 2026 23:52, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Was Ezri Konsa's challenge on Dan Ballard enough for Sunderland to be awarded a penalty? A furious Mikel Arteta described Sunderland's penalty in Arsenal's 2-0 win at the Stadium of Light as "unacceptable". The home side were awarded a spot kick in the 54th minute when defender Ezri Konsa was adjudged to have held Sunderland's Dan Ballard by referee John Brooks. "The referee's call of penalty to Sunderland for a holding offence by Konsa on Ballard was checked and confirmed by VAR," said a statement published by the Premier League Match Centre. The statement continued by quoting the interaction between on-pitch referee Brooks and the VAR. messages.text: Brits Skupski, Hewett clinch respective US Open doubles, wheelchair titles

metadata.summary: There was double success for Britain at the US Open on Saturday, with Alfie Hewett regaining his wheelchair singles title and Neal Skupski finally claiming the men’s doubles crown.
metadata.content: US Open 2026: Brits Neal Skupski, Alfie Hewett clinch respective doubles, wheelchair titles at Flushing Meadows | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open 2026: Brits Neal Skupski, Alfie Hewett clinch respective doubles, wheelchair titles at Flushing Meadows Britain’s Alfie Hewett regained his US Open wheelchair singles title with victory in Saturday’s final; compatriot Neal Skupski clinched men’s doubles title; watch US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, NOW and Sky Sports app Saturday 12 September 2026 23:08, UK Image: Britain's Neal Skupski (right) celebrates US Open doubles glory with playing partner Christian Harrison There was double success for Britain at the US Open on Saturday, with Alfie Hewett regaining his wheelchair singles title and Neal Skupski finally claiming the men’s doubles crown. Emotional Hewett burst into tears after beating Tokito Oda 6-0 7-6 (7-5) to deny the 20-year-old Japanese star a calendar Grand Slam. The 28-year-old, who was beaten by Oda in the finals of the French Open and Wimbledon this year, said: "It's taken lot of hard work, a lot of soul-searching at times, a lot of reflecting. "The Wimbledon pumping was a tough one to swallow. I definitely came away from that one with a lot of regret, took some time off and had a hard, long look in the mirror about who I wanted to be on the tennis court and how I wanted to show up.
